questions.prompt: Should SpecialistAssignment assign every approved work item or only work in the current ready DAG frontier?
questions.rationale: Assignment intent is stable planning data, while readiness is dynamic runtime state derived by Core.
options: Assign every approved work item, not only the current ready frontier (recommended)
Assign only the current ready frontier

questions.prompt: How many specialist profiles may be assigned to one work item in V1?
questions.rationale: A fixed cardinality keeps the handoff deterministic and avoids introducing collaboration orchestration into assignment.
options: Exactly one provider-neutral specialist profile per work item (recommended)
One or more collaborating profiles per work item

questions.prompt: Which boundary owns profile eligibility and ranking?
questions.rationale: Replaceable ranking is useful, but an extension cannot bypass required capabilities, tools, grants, or policy.
options: Core enforces hard capability, tool, grant, and policy constraints; a replaceable ranker chooses only among eligible profiles (recommended)
The configured ranker owns both eligibility and ranking

questions.prompt: What happens when one approved work item has no eligible specialist profile?
questions.rationale: Partial promotion could let an incomplete work plan reach execution.
options: Any unassignable work item blocks the complete candidate with needs-clarification; no partial baseline in V1 (recommended)
Promote assignments for eligible items and defer the rest

questions.prompt: Should SpecialistAssignment also schedule work, choose concrete AI models or humans, execute work, or modify the dependency DAG?
questions.rationale: Those effects belong to Core frontier control or WorkExecution rather than profile assignment.
options: Scheduling, availability, concrete runtime or model binding, execution, and DAG modification remain downstream (recommended)
Include runtime binding and scheduling in SpecialistAssignment
